Shushan-eduth--Lily of testimony. The lily is an emblem of beauty (see on <reference osisRef="Ps.45.1">Psa 45:1</reference>, title). As a description of the Psalm, those terms combined may denote a beautiful poem, witnessing--that is, for God's faithfulness as evinced in the victories referred to in the history cited. Aram-naharaim--Syria of the two rivers, or Mesopotamia beyond the river (Euphrates) (<reference osisRef="2Sam.10.16">2Sa 10:16</reference>). Aram-zobah--Syria of Zobah (<reference osisRef="2Sam.10.6">2Sa 10:6</reference>), to whose king the king of the former was tributary. The war with Edom, by Joab and Abishai (<reference osisRef="2Chr.18.12">2Ch 18:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Chr.18.25">25</reference>), occurred about the same time. Probably, while doubts and fears alternately prevailed respecting the issue of these wars, the writer composed this Psalm, in which he depicts, in the language of God's people, their sorrows under former disasters, offers prayer in present straits, and rejoices in confident hope of triumph by God's aid.</title> <div sID="gen9399" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6149"/>1-3. allude to disasters.<div eID="gen9399" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9400" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cast ... off--</hi>in scorn (<reference osisRef="Ps.43.2">Psa 43:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.44.9">44:9</reference>).<div eID="gen9400" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9401" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">scattered--</hi>broken our strength (compare <reference osisRef="2Sam.5.20">2Sa 5:20</reference>).<div eID="gen9401" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9402" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Oh, turn thyself--</hi>or, "restore to us" (prosperity).
